layers.face: The estate’s groom, in his fifties, thirty years at Maplegate — longer than any tenant. He speaks little, not twenty words in a day, and each one carries. He met you at the station: took your bag, drove the cart, no small talk the whole way, and at the gate left you three words, Martha’s inside, before leading the horse off.
layers.inside: His loyalty is to the estate itself — not to any one lord, but to this land, this stable, the bloodline of the horses, grown out of thirty years of work. He is also a quiet source of what the estate knows: a horse does not lie, and its state tells him where its rider has been. Action earns his trust where words do not — mending the stable roof does more than ten conversations.
layers.archetype: In Valewisp the groom is an inherited post, the steward’s equal in his own domain: you keep the house, he keeps the stable, each to his own, and they close ranks the moment it matters. Rational feudalism writes every person’s place into a contract; a man like him is the order that gathers outside it, out of years and craft. The morning you come for your horse and find it already in the right stall, the tack on the near hook, no word said — you have become one of his own.

marta.title: Martha
marta.subtitle: Head of the kitchen
marta.silhouette: The one who runs the kitchen

layers.face: The estate’s cook, in her forties, a big voice and a bigger laugh, plain and direct. The kitchen is hers, always flour on the apron; you were looked over head to foot the moment you came in.
layers.inside: She is the estate’s unofficial clearing-house — the gossip, the grievances, the small troubles all run through her kitchen. Little in the district moves without her knowing it, and whether she says so depends on whether you ask and whether it is worth the telling. The big voice makes her seem unable to keep a thing, which is its own cover: she always says less than she knows.
layers.archetype: On a Valewisp estate the kitchen is often the true hub of the house: masters come and go, the hearth stays lit. The whole of the duchy’s standing rests on hospitality, and the one who can read a guest, and the order a table is served in, holds not authority but news and goodwill. The day she remembers what you will not eat and quietly cooks to your taste without a word — that is her way with people.

layers.face: The maid of the main house — cleaning, laundry, the linen, and the tidying of the office besides. Quick, quiet, sparing with words and sometimes hesitant; she barely spoke showing you up to the room, but the eyes are sharp.
layers.inside: The rooms and the papers on the desks all pass under her hands, so more reaches her than a maid is credited with seeing. She knows more than she says — that faded rectangle on your desk, she would know what used to stand there.
layers.archetype: Whoever keeps the rooms is the estate’s quietest archive: rational feudalism sets everything down on paper, and the one who dusts the paper sees the whole house without being seen. She knows the most, and can say the least.

layers.face: The community master for the district north of Valehold, serving the estates of Maplegate, Thornwall and Millridge, past fifty. In the Temple Forged by the Sacred Flame the clergy are craftsmen, not pastors; what he keeps is the fire in the hearth, and he does not preach.
layers.inside: He keeps the vigil at the forge-chapel on Thursdays. He presses no belief on anyone; he treats the fire as a thing that ought to be tended. Weddings, funerals, a quarrel between neighbours — people mostly bring them to him first. He could have stayed at the capital’s sanctum and risen; in the end he chose to come home.
layers.archetype: In Valewisp faith is closer to respect for the natural order than to doctrine, and the master is what that looks like: at the kingdom’s centre the institution is a sanctum and a minting seal; here it is one man keeping a fire. When a life ends in this district, it is he who returns it to the flame. He knows a great deal, and offers none of it unasked.

layers.face: The lady of Thornwall, in her sixties, silver hair kept without a strand loose. You will most likely meet her at the hunt or a dinner — she need not raise her voice to still a room.
layers.inside: She has Valehold’s ways by heart: which household is due a call, which dinner cannot be missed. She is measured with people and remembers a kindness, and she takes the measure of a person by whether they listened before they spoke. Her word carries: someone she will vouch for needs little other proof.
layers.archetype: The baroness is a hub of Valewisp’s noble society and its quiet arbiter — to miss the hunt is to say something is wrong, and it is usually the lady of the house who arranges these occasions. She has lived in the valley long enough to have watched two generations of it change, and to know that each year’s fire is not the same fire.

layers.face: The Baron of Millridge, a little past forty. Always smiling, always proposing something — it was his letter that drew you into the hunt. His warmth is easy as sunlight, and does not quite outlast his turning away.
layers.inside: What he minds is the woods, the hunting ground, and appearances, and he is the season’s most active host: a farther stag, a new trail, another dish at dinner — and in the gaps of the talk, a small bargain quietly closed. Whether his invitation is a welcome or a way to keep the new steward where he can be watched is worth your weighing.
layers.archetype: He is the kind of baron who knows the web of contract by heart and turns it to his own account without once breaking a rule — harder to deal with than a man who breaks them, because you cannot tell him from the system itself. Every noble here owes duties upward and a guarantee downward, the way Baron von Alde stood surety for you; Henk only reads that web of favour and interest closer than most.

rational_feudalism.title: Rational Feudalism
rational_feudalism.subtitle: Kingdom of Marigni
rational_feudalism.text: What sets the Kingdom of Marigni apart: monarch, council and parliament coexist, and feudal contracts run inside a modern legal frame. It is ancient, restrained, intensely private, its politics unbroken since medieval times. The currency is the Guldmark. The guarantee letter between you and Baron von Alde is this system in its everyday form — favour and law in force at once.

sacred_flame.title: Temple Forged by the Sacred Flame
sacred_flame.subtitle: Marigni’s faith
sacred_flame.text: It venerates the Sacred Fire and the act of forging — the self as raw iron to be shaped. Its clergy are masters and forge-keepers, not pastors; a place of worship has a hearth, not an altar, the fire set into the floor at the centre. At the kingdom’s heart it is institution — sanctum, minting seal, the authentication of contracts; here in Valewisp it is closer to respect for the seasons and the natural order.

valewisp_duchy.title: Valewisp
valewisp_duchy.subtitle: The river duchy
valewisp_duchy.silhouette: The duchy you are bound for
valewisp_duchy.text: Marigni’s largest duchy — a temperate valley, rich farmland, mixed woods. Its economy is grain, timber, livestock, a little wine. It prizes courtesy, bloodline and the rhythm of the seasons — to be hasty is an insult, to be idle no more forgivable; time runs by season, not by clock. It thinks itself the most noble of the duchies: not from arrogance, but from living closest to the order of the land.

maplegate.title: Maplegate
maplegate.subtitle: North of Valehold
maplegate.silhouette: The estate you are to keep
maplegate.text: A middling estate in the district north of Valehold, Baron von Alde’s holding. Stone walls, timber tiles, an avenue of maples burning with autumn. The last steward left suddenly, with no handover at all; the harvest is near and the estate’s work has stood three weeks. You have thirty days.

millridge.title: Millridge
millridge.text: An estate in the valley. You have heard the name, and no more than that.
